0.long_answer: The muscle in question is the extensor digitorum brevis. This muscle is located on the dorsum of the foot and is primarily responsible for extending the second through fourth toes at their metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. It receives innervation from both the deep peroneal nerve and, in cases of anatomical variation, from the accessory deep peroneal nerve. This dual innervation explains why it is often the subject of discussion in studies focusing on anatomical variations of the peroneal nerve branches.
